lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Healthy Eating and Nutrition
lesson.summary: Food groups, amounts, nutrients and where our food comes from.
learning_objectives: Name food groups and what they do for the body
Explain how plants make food and animals find it

standards.text: Identify that animals, including humans, need the right types and amount of nutrition, and that they cannot make their own food; they get nutrition from what they eat

success_criteria: I can say what carbohydrates, protein and fibre do
I can read a food label
I can build a balanced plate
lesson.real_life: Packing a healthy lunch, reading labels and planning sehri and iftar meals.

warm_up.prompt: What do plants need to make food?
warm_up.explanation: Plants use light to make food.

warm_up.prompt: Water is important for our bodies.

blocks.markdown: Today we explore **nutrients** and healthy eating.
blocks.say: Welcome, young scientist! Today we explore what is in our food. We also read labels and build a balanced plate.

blocks.alt: Fruit and vegetables, bread and milk.
blocks.caption: Fruit and vegetables, bread and milk.

blocks.markdown: **Carbohydrates** give energy. **Protein** helps growth and repair.
blocks.say: Food gives us nutrients. Carbohydrates give us energy. Protein helps us grow and repair. Fats store energy. Vitamins and minerals keep us healthy.

blocks.alt: Carrots, mushrooms, a pepper, an onion and a tomato on a wooden table
blocks.caption: Vegetables give vitamins, minerals and fibre.
blocks.credit: Photo by engin akyurt on Unsplash
blocks.say: Fibre helps our digestion, and water is essential for life. These vegetables give us vitamins, minerals and fibre.

scenes.caption: Carbohydrates: energy.
scenes.say: Bread, rice and roti are carbohydrates. They give us energy to run and play.

scenes.caption: Protein: growth and repair.
scenes.say: Eggs, fish and daal have protein. It helps us grow and repair our muscles.

question.prompt: Which nutrient gives us energy to be active?

blocks.markdown: Plants are **producers**: they make their own food.
blocks.say: Plants are producers. They make their own food in their leaves, using sunlight. Animals cannot, so they eat plants or other animals.

blocks.alt: Plants make food. Animals eat plants.
blocks.caption: Plants make food. Animals eat plants.

question.prompt: Animals can make their own food from sunlight.
question.explanation: Animals must eat plants or other animals.

blocks.title: The canteen robot
blocks.transcript: A school canteen robot wants to build a plate. It has lots of food. The robot piles on sweets. Is that a good plate? Not really. Now it adds lots of fruit and vegetables. They fill a big part of the plate. Next, roti and rice. They give energy to learn and play. A smaller share of daal, eggs and yoghurt helps muscles grow. And one small treat. A little bit is fine. The robot adds a glass of water. Our bodies need water every day. A balanced plate. Big bread, big vegetables, small sweets. Well done, robot!
blocks.caption: A canteen robot learns why bread is big and sweets are small.

points: Plants make food. Animals eat it
blocks.say: Remember. Food gives us nutrients. A mix of foods gives us what our bodies need.

blocks.markdown: A **label** shows nutrition information per 100 grams.
blocks.say: Most packed foods have a label. It shows how much fat, sugar and salt is in 100 grams. That helps us compare foods fairly.

scenes.caption: Snack A: 18 g sugar.
scenes.say: Snack A has 18 grams of sugar in every 100 grams. That is a lot.

scenes.caption: Snack B: 7 g sugar.
scenes.say: Snack B has only 7 grams of sugar in 100 grams. Snack B has less sugar.

question.prompt: Why are labels given per 100 grams?

options.text: So we can compare foods fairly

blocks.markdown: Traffic light colours show if a food is **high** or low in fat, sugar and salt.
blocks.say: Compare two snacks by looking at sugar, fat and salt. Red means high, amber is medium and green means low. Check the serving size too.

blocks.title: Sort the snacks
blocks.goal: Sort the foods into a lot of sugar and less sugar.

materials: Clean food packets or pictures of labels
instructions: Find the sugar amount per 100 g on two snacks.

question.explanation: Many fizzy and juice drinks have a lot of sugar.

points: Red means high, green means low
blocks.say: Remember. Labels help us compare foods. Hidden sugar, fat and salt can add up, so check the label.

terms.meaning: A sign on a food packet with information.

blocks.markdown: A **balanced diet** has the right amounts of different foods.
blocks.say: A balanced diet has a mix of foods in the right amounts. The biggest parts are fruit and vegetables, and starchy foods such as rice, roti and bread.

blocks.alt: A ring of colourful fruit and vegetables around a wooden board
blocks.caption: Fruit and vegetables should fill a big part of the plate.
blocks.credit: Photo by engin akyurt on Unsplash
blocks.say: This colourful spread of fruit and vegetables should fill a big part of the plate. Protein and dairy are smaller parts. Oils and sweet treats are the smallest.

question.prompt: Which foods should make up the biggest parts of the plate?
question.hint: Think of roti, rice and salad.
question.explanation: Fruit, vegetables and starchy foods fill most of the plate.

blocks.markdown: Aim for **five a day**: five portions of fruit and vegetables.
blocks.say: Plan meals for a day. For sehri or breakfast, try wholegrain bread and yoghurt. For iftar, dates and water, then roti, daal and sabzi.

scenes.caption: Breakfast.
scenes.say: Breakfast: wholegrain bread, an egg and a tomato.

scenes.caption: Dinner.
scenes.say: Dinner: roti, daal and vegetables. A mix of food groups.

blocks.title: Food match
blocks.say: Flip the cards and find the matching pairs. A little brain break!

question.prompt: A child has eaten 3 portions of fruit and vegetables. How many more to reach five a day?

points: Fill most of the plate with fruit, vegetables and starchy foods
Have smaller amounts of protein and dairy
Have only a little oil, sugar and salt
blocks.say: Remember. A balanced diet means the right amounts, not equal amounts. Treats are fine in small amounts.

terms.meaning: A mix of foods in the right amounts.
Five portions of fruit and vegetables each day.
Foods such as rice, roti and bread that give energy.
Foods made from milk, such as yoghurt.
Foods we enjoy sometimes in small amounts.

blocks.markdown: Many foods come from **crops** grown in fields.
blocks.say: Much of our food starts as a plant. Wheat grows in a field. It is made into flour for bread and roti.

blocks.alt: A loaf of rustic bread beside a pile of wheat grains
blocks.caption: Wheat grains become flour and bread.
blocks.credit: Photo by Ca D. on Unsplash
blocks.say: Wheat grains are ground into flour. Seasonal food is picked at its best time of year, and local food travels fewer food miles.

question.prompt: Which food is made from wheat?
question.explanation: Bread is made from wheat flour.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Not all fat is bad

blocks.markdown: Some **fat** is needed. Too much is not healthy.
blocks.say: Our bodies need some fat for energy and to take in some vitamins. Too much fat is the problem, not all fat.

blocks.alt: Nuts, olive oil and fish have healthy fats.
blocks.caption: Nuts, olive oil and fish have healthy fats.

blocks.prompt: Is a ready meal always worse than a home-cooked meal? Have a think first.
blocks.answer_markdown: Not always, but ready meals can have more salt, fat or sugar. Read the label and compare.

question.prompt: Our bodies need a small amount of fat.
question.explanation: Some fat is an essential part of a healthy diet.

blocks.alt: Growing your own vegetables in pots.
blocks.caption: Growing your own vegetables in pots.
blocks.say: You can grow vegetables yourself, even in pots. Fresh food from your own garden has no food miles at all.

points: Food comes from plants and animals
Seasonal and local food is a good choice
Some fat is needed, but not too much
blocks.say: Remember. Food comes from plants and animals. All nutrients matter, in the right amounts.
